incident-bot: INCIDENT detected: increased 5xx rate from smart-routing service. symptom=tool_call_failures, metric=err_rate>5% over 2m. paging oncall @sara :rotating_light:

sara (oncall): seeing the alert, joining. on it.

olivia (support): multiple customers reporting 'tool call not supported' errors in the last 10m — Support ticket cluster #4562. Primarily chat endpoints that use function/tool calling.

mike (infra): digging into routing logs — requests are bouncing between us-east-1 and eu-west-1. I see a lot of retries with different model_variant ids. Could be fallback loop.

julia (runtime): quick theory: we recently onboarded a quantized variant (q_v2) that is FP8/INT8 and does not have tool-calling shims compiled. If the smart-router falls back to q_v2 when fp16 variant is overloaded, requests with toolcalls will error out, trigger fallback policy again -> loop.

kevin (eng-sre): confirmed in trace: request->us-east-1(fp16_v1) returns ENOTSUP when heavy; router falls back to eu-west-1(q_v2) which responds 400/UNSUPPORTED_TOOL_CALL, causing router to try a different variant, then back to us-east-1, repeat. Counted ~7 hops for some sessions.

raj (ml): that matches model compatibility metadata being wrong. Our compatibility matrix indicates q_v2 supports tool_call:true for some endpoints — looks like the metadata flag was set at onboarding but the runtime doesn't have the hook.

olivia (support): customers impacted: 3 enterprise customers showing higher error rates, one is in EMEA. SLA risk if not fixed in 30m.

sara (oncall): escalate. I'll take incident lead. Immediate mitigation options?

mike (infra): quick mitigation: disable cross-region fallback in smart-routing policy so we don't loop across regions. Then route all tool-calling requests to a safe variant tag (fp16_v1) in-region. I can flip policy now.

julia (runtime): prefer we blacklist q_v2 for tool_call endpoints instead — that's lower blast radius. Also need to mark q_v2 as tool_call:false in model registry to prevent router choosing it in the future.

kevin (eng-sre): agreed. I'll patch the routing policy and add a temporary predicate: if request.features.tool_call==true then candidate.exclude_tags contains "quantized". Command: 
```
# temp disable quantized fallback for tool-calls
rci update-policy smart-routing --policy-id=sr-global --patch '{"rules": [{"when": "features.tool_call==true","exclude_tags": ["quantized"]}]}'
```
Applying now.

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty alert escalated to SRE rotation.

kevin (eng-sre): applied patch in prod, 2s ago. Monitoring error rate.

mike (infra): after patch, region hop count dropped. 5xx rate down from 6.2% to 1.1% in the last 60s. Latency slightly up for some fp16 nodes but stable.

olivia (support): notifying affected customers that we have mitigated the loop and are investigating root cause.

julia (runtime): root cause confirmed: q_v2 binary built without tool-call adapters. Compatibility metadata incorrectly flagged it as tool compatible. Repro in staging: call to tool endpoint on q_v2 -> payload validation passes but runtime returns 501 UNSUPPORTED_TOOL_CALL.

raj (ml): found last onboarding commit for q_v2 registry entry: had metadata {"tool_call": "true", "context_len": "32k"} but the build tag was different. Looks like a manual override slipped in during upload.

sara (oncall): action plan: (1) keep the routing predicate in place for 2 hours, (2) update model registry to reflect tool_call:false for q_v2, (3) roll a patched q_v2 build with tool-call shim if we want it supported, (4) postmortem + add pre-check to onboarding.

kevin (eng-sre): making registry change now (write-only metadata):
```
modelctl set-metadata q_v2 tool_call false --reason "runtime lacks shim"
```
Done. Router picks that up after 30s.

mike (infra): pushing a safer global policy so that future quantized variants are excluded by default for tool-calls. Will open PR to change default policy template.

olivia (support): customer update sent. One customer asked for ETA on a proper q_v2 fix — told them ETA 48h for a patched build or to use fp16_v1 in the meantime.

julia (runtime): I'm starting a build of q_v2 with tool-call enabled (compile flag --enable-tool-adapters). Will run validation tests for the shim. If green, can promote in 24-48h.

raj (ml): we'll add an automated compatibility test: when registry metadata claims tool_call:true, onboarding pipeline will run a minimal tool_call smoke test against the runtime binary. Failing that, reject registry entry. I'll open PR.

sara (oncall): handoff plan: I'll stay on for 30m to monitor, then hand to mike for overnight. Please summarize your takeaways in chat so I can include in the incident record.

kevin (eng-sre): takeaway: mis-specified model metadata caused router to select an incompatible quantized variant, which triggered region fallback loops. Immediate fix: exclude quantized variants for tool-calls + correct registry metadata. Longer-term: add onboarding checks and default policy template changes.

julia (runtime): takeaway: runtime should expose capability flags at build time and onboarding must ingest them automatically; patching q_v2 is in progress.

mike (infra): takeaway: router policies need canaries for cross-region fallbacks to avoid loops; implementing a hop-count limit as well.

olivia (support): takeaway: notify customers early, provide guidance to pin to known-good variants.

pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by SRE rotation. Escalation cleared.

incident-bot: INCIDENT resolved: err_rate below threshold and loop mitigated by policy patch. Recording timeline to incident tracker.

sara (oncall): creating JIRA INC-789 to track follow-ups: registry pre-check PR, default policy template PR, runtime build for q_v2, add hop-count limit to router. Assigning owners.

kevin (eng-sre): leaving a note: we should add telemetry alert that watches for high hop counts per session and auto-throttle fallback frequency.

mike (infra): handing off to night oncall @mike (infra). I'll run 1h of post-mitigation monitoring then hand to next rotation.

sara (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll close the page after the follow-ups are logged. :white_check_mark:
